items.prompt: 原题 1：Why does Dr. Kline state that he is “the enemy” in the first sentence? According to him, who thinks he is the enemy?

A Scientist: I Am the Enemy
Ronald M. Kline M.D.

(1) I am the enemy! One of those hated, cold-hearted physician-scientists involved in animal research. How strange, for I have never thought of myself as an evil person. I became a pediatrician because of my love for children and my desire to keep them healthy. During medical school and residency, however, I saw many children die of leukemia, prematurity, and traumatic injury—circumstances against which medicine has made tremendous progress, but still has far to go. More important, I also saw children, alive and healthy, thanks to advances in medical science such as infant respirators, strong antibiotics, new surgical techniques, and the entire field of organ transplantation. My desire to tip the scales in favor of healthy, happy children drew me to medical research.

(2) My accusers claim that I torture animals for the sole purpose of advancing my career. My experiments supposedly have no relevance to medicine and are easily replaced by computer simulation. Meanwhile, an apathetic public barely watches, convinced that the issue has no significance, and publicity-conscious politicians increasingly give way to the demands of the activists.

(3) We in medical research have also been unacceptably apathetic. We have allowed the most extreme animal-rights protesters to seize the initiative and frame the issue as one of “animal fraud.” We have been complacent in our belief that a knowledgeable public would sense the importance of animal research to the public health. Perhaps we have been mistaken in not responding to the emotional tone of the argument created by those sad posters of animals by waving equally sad posters of children dying of leukemia or cystic fibrosis.

(4) Much is made of the pain caused to these animals in the name of medical science. The animal-rights activists contend that this is evidence of our cruel and brutal nature. A more reasonable argument, however, can be advanced in our defense. Life is often cruel, both to animals and human beings. Teenagers get thrown from the back of a pickup truck and suffer severe head injuries. Toddlers, barely able to walk, find themselves at the bottom of a swimming pool while a parent checks the mail. Physicians hoping to alleviate the pain and suffering that these tragedies cause have but three choices: create an animal model of the injury or disease and use that model to understand the process and test new therapies, experiment on human beings—some experiments will succeed, most will fail—or finally, leave medical knowledge unchanged, hoping that accidental discoveries will lead us to the advances.

(5) Some animal-rights activists would suggest a fourth choice, claiming that computer models can simulate animal experiments, thus making the actual experiments unnecessary. Computers can simulate, reasonably well, the effects of well-understood principles on complex systems, as in the application of the laws of physics to airplane and automobile design. However, when the principles themselves are in question, as is the case with the complex biological systems under study, computer modeling alone is of little value.

(6) One of the terrifying effects of the effort to restrict the use of animals in medical research is that its impact will not be felt for many years and decades: drugs that might have been discovered will not be; surgical techniques that might have been developed will not be; and fundamental biological processes that might have been understood will remain mysteries. There is the danger that self-serving political solutions will be found to satisfy a vocal minority, while the consequences of those decisions will not be apparent until long after the decisions are made and the decision-making forgotten.

(7) Fortunately, most of us enjoy good health, and the tragedy of watching one’s child die has become a rare experience. Yet our good fortune should not make us unappreciative of the health we enjoy or the advances that make it possible. Vaccines, antibiotics, insulin, and drugs to treat heart disease, hypertension, and stroke are all based on animal research. Most complex surgical procedures, such as coronary-artery bypass and organ transplantation, are initially developed in animals. Presently undergoing animal studies are techniques to insert genes in humans in order to replace the defective ones found to be the cause of so much disease. These studies will effectively end if animal research is severely restricted.

(8) In America today, death has become an event isolated from our daily existence—out of the sight and thoughts of most of us. As a doctor who has watched many children die, and their parents grieve, I am particularly angered by people capable of so much compassion for a dog or a cat, but with seemingly so little for a dying human being. These people seem so insulated from the reality of human life and death and what it means.

(9) Make no mistake, however: I am not advocating the needlessly cruel treatment of animals. To the extent that the animal-rights movement has made us more aware of the needs of these animals and made us search harder for suitable alternatives, they have made a significant contribution. But if the more radical members of this movement are successful in limiting further research, their efforts will bring about a tragedy that will cost many lives. The real question is whether an apathetic majority can be aroused to protect its future against a vocal, but misdirected, minority.

Source: Adapted from Kline, Ronald M. “A Scientist: I Am the Enemy.”

原文词注：residency = the period in which a doctor continues training in a hospital after completing medical school；leukemia = a type of cancer that affects the blood stream, often causing death；prematurity = being born before the body’s organs are developed enough to allow normal survival；traumatic = seriously damaging；respirators = devices to help people breathe；transplantation = replacement of a body part, usually donated from another person；cystic fibrosis = a serious medical condition that makes breathing and eating difficult；decades = groups of ten；hypertension = abnormally high blood pressure。

(1) The rapidly rising cost of higher education is causing many to question the value of continuing education beyond high school. Many wonder whether the high cost of tuition, the cost of choosing college over full-time employment, and the accumulation of thousands of dollars of debt is, in the long run, worth the investment. Practice 6对应原文

Paragraph 6
One of the terrifying effects of the effort to restrict the use of animals in medical research is that its impact will not be felt for many years and decades: drugs that might have been discovered will not be; surgical techniques that might have been developed will not be; and fundamental biological processes that might have been understood will remain mysteries. There is the danger that self-serving political solutions will be found to satisfy a vocal minority, while the consequences of those decisions will not be apparent until long after the decisions are made and the decision-making forgotten.

Paragraph 7
Fortunately, most of us enjoy good health, and the tragedy of watching one’s child die has become a rare experience. Yet our good fortune should not make us unappreciative of the health we enjoy or the advances that make it possible. Vaccines, antibiotics, insulin, and drugs to treat heart disease, hypertension, and stroke are all based on animal research. Most complex surgical procedures, such as coronary-artery bypass and organ transplantation, are initially developed in animals. Presently undergoing animal studies are techniques to insert genes in humans in order to replace the defective ones found to be the cause of so much disease. These studies will effectively end if animal research is severely restricted.

Paragraph 8
In America today, death has become an event isolated from our daily existence—out of the sight and thoughts of most of us. As a doctor who has watched many children die, and their parents grieve, I am particularly angered by people capable of so much compassion for a dog or a cat, but with seemingly so little for a dying human being. These people seem so insulated from the reality of human life and death and what it means.

rules.title: 论证的组成
rules.explanation: 争议背景→明确立场→理由与证据→counterargument→rebuttal→结论。论证不是情绪化争吵，也不是只列正方理由。
rules.example: 原创示例：Although online classes offer flexibility, some tasks still benefit from face-to-face interaction.
steps: 先用一句话写清可以争论的问题，再写作者主张；主张应说明赞成什么或反对什么，不能只是介绍话题。
为主张列出至少一个理由，再补可核查的事实、例子或研究作为支持；检查证据是否真的能推出该理由。
替对方写出一个公平、具体的反对理由，接着解释其证据或适用范围为何不足；结尾回到自己的主张。

breakdown.note: 让步：先承认线上课堂灵活这一优点，使对方观点被准确呈现。although 引导的部分不能单独当完整句。

breakdown.text: some tasks still benefit from face-to-face interaction.
breakdown.note: 主句提出作者的有限主张：某些任务仍受益于面对面交流。下一步要说明哪些任务、为什么；这句话本身还不是充分证据。

rules.pitfall: 只写“我同意”或列优点还不够；也不要把 although 后的让步误认成作者最终立场。对方观点、回应和证据要分得清。

check.prompt: 【原创理解检查】作者主张“学校应保留部分面授课”，哪一句最适合作为需要回应的反方理由？

options.label: 线上课能减少通勤，对远距离学生更方便。
学校应保留部分面授课。

check.explanation: A 给出支持另一种安排的理由，可以据此讨论方便与教学任务的权衡。B 与争点关联弱；C 只重复作者主张，没有形成反方理由。

rules.sourceLabel: 教材 Argumentative Essays 书页 147、155、160（PDF 2、10、15 页）；讲解例句与理解检查为原创。

rules.title: Block 与 point-by-point
rules.explanation: block：反方与反驳集中一组，己方论证集中另一组；point-by-point：每一重点下呈现反方、反驳和证据。两种都要让读者知道作者最终立场。
rules.example: 原创示例：Cost objection → response; quality objection → response.
steps: 先列争论中的几个具体问题，如费用、质量、时间；为每个问题配上反方理由、自己的回应和支持。
选 block 时，把反方与回应集中在一组段落，再用另一组段落展开己方理由；选 point-by-point 时，每个问题就近完成反方—回应—证据。
用段落提纲检查读者能否看出每一条回应针对什么，以及作者最后支持哪一方。教材图示是常见安排，实际文章可以调整顺序。

breakdown.note: 围绕费用这个问题，先呈现质疑，再紧接着回应；这是一组局部论证。
转到质量时再完成另一组质疑和回应。因此原示例体现逐点处理；若把所有质疑放一起、己方支持另起一组，则更接近 block。

rules.pitfall: 不要把“段落数量”当成两种结构的区别。核心是双方材料如何编排；逐点式也可以先写己方主张，再写反方与反驳。

check.prompt: 【原创理解检查】一篇文章先在费用段讨论反方与回应，再在质量段讨论反方与回应，属于哪种主要安排？

options.label: Point-by-point：逐个问题就近处理双方观点。
Block：全部反方和全部己方必须分成两个整块。
没有引用数字，所以不能判断组织方式。

check.explanation: 按费用、质量分别对照双方，是逐点式。是否使用数字影响证据力度，不决定文章的组织方式。

rules.sourceLabel: 教材书页 156–157（PDF 11–12 页）；示意与理解检查为原创。

rules.title: 框定争议与受众
rules.explanation: 引言交代双方争点和作者判断。考虑supportive/neutral/antagonistic读者；不同受众需要不同背景与证据，但不能歪曲对方观点。
rules.example: 原创示例：Some students question the cost of university, while others emphasize its long-term value.
steps: 用中性语言交代争议的两边，避免在介绍对方时先贴贬义标签；随后给出自己的可讨论立场。
设想读者是支持、尚未决定还是反对：他们已经知道什么，又最可能追问什么？把这些问题写在提纲旁。
为读者的主要疑问准备合适的解释和证据。支持者也需要理由；中立和反对者通常更需要可核查的支持，情绪化措辞不能代替证据。

breakdown.text: Some students question the cost of university,
breakdown.note: 先呈现一方关切：大学费用是否值得。question 在这里是质疑，不等于“完全反对大学”。

breakdown.text: while others emphasize its long-term value.
breakdown.note: while 表对照，呈现另一方关切。整句说明争议的两面，但还没有明确作者选择哪一边；引言下一句需要补自己的判断。

rules.pitfall: 把双方说完不等于已经写出 thesis。迎合受众也不等于删掉不利证据；应改变解释重点，不应歪曲对方。

check.prompt: 【原创理解检查】“Some students worry about tuition, while others value the degree.” 单独作引言结尾时，最需要补充什么？

options.label: 作者对争议的明确判断，以及后文将支持的方向。
再重复一遍两种人的人数。
把反对方称作无知的人。

check.explanation: 原句只框定争议，读者还不知道作者最终立场。人数可能成为证据，但不能自动替代主张；攻击人也不是论证。

rules.sourceLabel: 教材书页 158、161–162（PDF 13、16–17 页）；例句与理解检查为原创。

rules.title: 让步与反驳
rules.explanation: 可以指出证据不充分、承认部分合理再说明局限，或权衡双方后坚持立场。避免稻草人，反驳针对理由而非攻击持论者。
rules.example: 原创示例：Admittedly, the course is expensive. However, its flexible schedule can reduce travel costs.
steps: 先准确复述反方的一条理由，判断其中是否存在你可以承认的事实；承认局部事实不等于接受对方全部结论。
选择合适回应：指出证据不足，承认优点再说明局限，或权衡双方后解释哪个因素更重要。具体说清反驳针对哪一步推论。
补上事实、例子或限定条件支撑回应，检查有没有攻击说话者、夸大对方主张或仅用 however 宣布反对。

breakdown.note: Admittedly 标出让步：承认课程费用高。句子到句号结束，先让承认的内容完整成立。

breakdown.text: However, its flexible schedule can reduce travel costs.
breakdown.note: However 转向回应：灵活安排可能节省交通费。can 表可能的好处，不保证总成本一定更低；还需比较实际费用。

rules.pitfall: 转折词本身不会产生反驳。承认“贵”后说“很好”太空泛；要说明另一项成本或收益怎样改变结论，且不能把“可能节省”写成“必然划算”。

check.prompt: 【原创理解检查】反方说“这门课学费高，因此绝不值得上”，哪项回应最符合让步后限定结论？

options.label: 学费确实高，但若省下的通勤与住宿费足够多，总费用仍可能较低。
提出这个问题的人都很懒。

check.explanation: A 承认学费事实，再以明确条件检验“绝不值得”的过强结论。B 攻击人，C 只有连接词，都没有回应推理。

rules.sourceLabel: 教材书页 162–164（PDF 17–19 页）；例句与理解检查为原创。

rules.title: 情态动词与短语情态
rules.explanation: should建议，must强要求，may/might可能，could可能/建议；后接动词原形。be able to/have to/ought to按各自结构，be/have随主语与时态变化。
rules.example: 原创示例：Students should evaluate evidence carefully.
steps: 先决定要表达建议、义务、许可、能力还是可能性，再选 should、must、may、might、could 等；不要仅凭中文“能”机械对应一个词。
情态动词后直接接动词原形：should evaluate，不能写 should to evaluate，也不能给 evaluate 加 s。若接被动，用 be + 过去分词。
改成短语情态时按结构变化：be able to、have to、be allowed to、ought to 等。be/have 需要随主语和时态变化，而且不同表达的语气不一定完全相同。

breakdown.note: 主语是复数名词，说明是谁执行动作。情态动词本身不会因此加 s。
表示建议或应当，强度通常不同于 must；本句是在建议怎样处理证据。
should 后用 evaluate 原形，不加 to。evidence 是宾语，carefully 说明评估方式。

rules.pitfall: should to do 是常见错误；ought to do 则必须保留 to。也不要把 must 的强义务和 might 的可能性当成可随意互换的同义表达。

check.prompt: 【原创理解检查】哪一句同时保持“学生应仔细核对证据”的建议语气与正确结构？

options.label: Students should check the evidence carefully.
Students should to check the evidence carefully.
Students should checks the evidence carefully.

check.explanation: should 后直接接动词原形 check。B 多了 to；C 错给动词加 s。

rules.title: 建议类虚拟语气
rules.explanation: suggest/recommend/require/insist等表示建议或要求时可用that + 主语 + 动词原形；否定为not + 原形，被动为be + 过去分词。注意suggest表示“表明”时不机械套虚拟。
rules.example: 原创示例：The committee recommends that the policy be revised.
rules.before: The committee recommends that the policy is revised.
rules.after: The committee recommends that the policy be revised.
steps: 先看主句是否在提出建议、要求或坚持某事应当发生；若 suggest 只是表示“迹象表明”，不能自动套用建议类虚拟。
在 that 从句中先放完整主语，再用动词原形。即使主语是单数，也不改成三单形式；否定放 not + 原形。
需要被动时用 be + 过去分词，例如 that the policy be revised。最后检查意思是否仍是“建议修改”，没有变成“描述已经修改”。

breakdown.note: 主句明确提出建议，因此后面的从句表达希望实施的安排。
that 引出建议内容，the policy 是从句主语；它是被修改的对象。
被动结构用 be 原形 + revised 过去分词。这里不用 is revised，因为不是单纯报告政策现状。

rules.pitfall: 不要因 the policy 是单数就写 is；建议类从句保留 be 原形。但在“证据表明……”的事实陈述里，也不要反过来误用这一结构。

check.prompt: 【原创理解检查】委员会建议延期审查，按本节句式应填：The committee recommends that the review ___ postponed.
check.explanation: recommend 在此提出建议，that 从句的被动式为 be postponed。be 保持原形。

rules.sourceLabel: 教材书页 154（PDF 9 页）；例句与理解检查为原创。

rules.title: 报告动词和词性
rules.explanation: claim/argue/assert指提出主张；concede承认部分；challenge/refute质疑/反驳。词性变化要适配句子，如benefit/beneficial、significance/significant。
rules.example: 原创示例：Critics challenge the claim, but supporters provide additional evidence.
steps: 先判断引述者在做什么：提出主张可用 argue/claim，承认局部理由可用 concede，质疑可用 challenge。选词要与原作者的态度和证据强度相符。
把引述来源和观点分开：Critics challenge... 告诉读者这是批评者的动作；不要把别人提出的 claim 写成已经证实的事实。
最后按句子位置检查词性和形式：形容词修饰名词，动词随时态和主语变化，可数名词检查单复数。不要只看到题干词根就原样填入。

breakdown.note: Critics 指出谁在行动；challenge 表示质疑这项主张，并未声称已经成功证伪。
but 连接另一方回应。provide evidence 表示给出支持；证据是否充分仍需读者检查，不能仅凭 additional 就断言观点正确。

rules.pitfall: refute 通常比 challenge 更强，不能把“提出质疑”随意改成“已驳倒”。词形题也要读整个句子：a therapeutic method 要形容词，而 receive therapy 要名词。

check.prompt: 【原创理解检查】根据句子位置，选择正确词形：The treatment has a ___ effect.
check.explanation: 空格位于冠词 a 与名词 effect 之间，需要修饰 effect 的形容词 therapeutic。therapy/therapies 是名词形式。
